airport.name: Rome–Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci International Airport

summary: Rome–Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (FCO) is Italy's largest and busiest airport, named after the Renaissance polymath Leonardo da Vinci. Located in the coastal town of Fiumicino approximately 30 km southwest of Rome's city center, it opened in 1961 and serves as the primary international gateway to Rome. It operates as the main hub for ITA Airways and handles over 40 million passengers annually across its terminals.
faqs:
Q: How far is Fiumicino Airport from central Rome?
A: FCO is located about 30 km southwest of Rome's city center, with travel times of 30–45 minutes depending on your chosen transport.

Q: What is the best way to get from FCO to Rome by train?
A: The Leonardo Express is a dedicated non-stop train service connecting the airport to Roma Termini Station in approximately 32 minutes, running every 15–30 minutes.

Q: How many terminals does Fiumicino Airport have?
A: FCO has three main passenger terminals: Terminal 1, Terminal 3, and Terminal 5. Check-in areas are organized by airline and destination.

Q: Is there free Wi-Fi available at FCO?
A: Yes, free Wi-Fi is available throughout all terminals and can be accessed by connecting to the 'Free Wi-Fi FCO' network
